content:
Let \(A,B\) be the original numbers. Decreasing every digit of \(A\) by \(1\) means replacing \(A\) by \(A-11111\).

Let \(D=A-B\), so \(S=|D|\).

Case 1: \(A\) is modified. Then
\[
|(A-11111)-B|=|D-11111|=10002.
\]
Thus
\[
D-11111=\pm 10002 \implies D=21113 \text{ or } 1109.
\]
Since \(S=|D|\) is four-digit, \(D=21113\) is impossible. Hence \(S=1109\).

Case 2: \(B\) is modified. Then
\[
|A-(B-11111)|=|D+11111|=10002,
\]
so
\[
D=-1109 \text{ or } -21113.
\]
Again the four-digit condition gives \(S=1109\).

This value is attainable, e.g. \(A=23332\), \(B=22223\):
\[
|23332-22223|=1109,
\]
and decreasing \(A\)'s digits gives
\[
|12221-22223|=10002.
\]

Therefore, the only possible value is

\[
\boxed{1109}
\]
